full_judgment:
2. Plaintiffs instituted the suit for declaration of 16 annas title over the property described in the schedule to the plaint. It is the plaint case that the suit land along with other lands were belonged to Krishna Chandra Das, Kali Charan Das, Dagu Charan Das and Boikuntha Chandra Das and their names were recorded in the settlement khatian in equal 4 annas share. The suit land, after the death of the aforesaid record tenants devolved upon Pach Kori Das. Pach Kori Das while possessing the aforesaid land after taking permission from the relevant authority as at that time law provides for such permission sold 36 decimals of land to plaintiff's predecessor by registered kabala deed No. 6270 executed on 6th Aswin , 1373 BS corresponding to 23-9-66 and registered on 22-10-66 and after purchase, predecessor of plain-tiff demarcated the suit land, after mutation, opened a new khatian in his name and paid regularly the rents and land development tax. Salimullah, the purchaser, was killed during liberation war leaving the plaintiff No.1 as widow, plaintiff Nos. 3, 4 and 7 as sons and plaintiff Nos. 2, 5, 6 and 8 as daughters. The plaintiffs enjoyed the suit land in ejmali. Plaintiffs passed a plan for construction of a multistoried building in some portion of the land from the relevant authority and in remaining portion of the land, plaintiff maintained his possession by constructing dwelling huts, by growing vegetables and also by rented some portion of the land to tenants. Plaintiffs regularly paying their rents and also the land development taxes. Plaintiffs paid rents and other taxes up to 1397 BS Khoshra RS khatian No. 478 was prepared in the name of Md. Salim Ullah and was published. But on receiving the RS khatian it appears that 3 decimals of land of dag No. 1019 and 15 decimals of land of dag No.102 have been wrongly recorded and published in the name of Pachkori Das in 8 annas share and Ramesh Chandra Das, Rajani Chandra Das, Nibaran Chandra Das and Rajkumar Chandra Das in 2 annas share each and recorded in the name of Government of India represented by Government of Bangladesh and it has been stated in the column that the lands vested as non resident property maintained by Government of Bangladesh represented by Sub Divisional Management Committee in 16 annas share. In the Khosra khatian, in respect of 10 decimals of land of RS dag No. 1019, it has been recorded in RS dag No. 1019 of RS khatian No. 478, in place of 10 decimals of land 3 decimals of land recorded, remaining 7 decimals of land was recorded in the name of defendant No.4 in RS dag No.1019. In respect of 25 decimals of land settlement dag Nos.692, 693 694 were prepared in khatian No.478 in the name of Md. Salimullah and it has been recorded as in dag No. 1022 for 15 decimals of land. This being totally wrong as the khatian was not prepared as per the requirement of law, plaintiffs filed the suit. 

 6. The case of defendant No. 4 is that, after the death of original owner, Krishna Chandra Das, Kalicharan Das, Dagu Charan Das and Boikuntha Chandra Das, Pachkori Das, son of, Dagu Charan Das became owner in 4 annas share. On an amicable partition, 10 decimal of land of CS dag No. 692, 67 decimals of land of CS khatian No. 693, 12 decimals of land of CS dag No. 694, in total 89 decimals of land fallen in favour of Pachkori Das. He being sole owner of the aforesaid land, in 1963 for road scheme of the Pourashava, certain portion of the land of Pachkori Das was fallen and by registered saf kabala deed NO. 3870 dated 30-5-1963. Pachkori sold 7 decimals of land towards north, out of 10 decimals of land of CS dag No.158 of khatian No.692 and 81/2 decimals of land towards north, out of 12 decimals of land of khatian No.694, by registered saf kabala deed No. 3214 dated 1-5-1963 to this defeadant. By registered deed No. 4877 deed No.4877 dated 8-8-1963, Pachkori Das sold 6 decimals of land towards south, 151/2 decimals of land from extreme West out of 67 decimals of land of dag No.191 of the aforesaid khatian to this defendant. Pachkori Das from 191 Masdair mouja, CS and SA Dag No. 692, 693, 694 by 3 separate deeds sold 37-2/3 decimals of land or Pourashava and delivered possession and Pourashava by cutting earth and by filling earth, constructed road and in remaining portion of the land established Masdir bazaar for the benefit of the local people and one storied building which was constructed was dismantle by Pourashava Magistrate with the help of police. Pourashava tried to demarcate the land of dag Nos. 692, 693, 694 but due to the hostile attitude of defendant Nos. 5 and 6, who did not cooperate the demarcation was not made.
